title: Discourse structure classification
measurement_method: Systematic stratified sample drawn every ~6-9th row by id within word-count terciles (short/medium/long), read context_raw + response_raw manually, multi-label classified against a predefined category list, then tabulated with Python (collections.Counter) and extrapolated to the full dataset by proportion.
claim_type: INFERRED (sampled and extrapolated; not a full-dataset count)
confidence_note: Confidence is medium-high for categories with sample_count >= 15 (stable proportions), medium for 6-14, low for < 6 (subject to sampling noise; a systematic 317-row sample gives roughly +/-5pp margin at 95% CI for a 20% proportion, wider for rarer categories).

discourse_by_response_length_bucket.note: Rows were stratified into terciles by response_word_count: short (<=5 words), medium (6-10 words), long (>10 words). Each bucket ~103-108 rows in the sample.
discourse_by_response_length_bucket.interpretation: INFERRED: as response length increases, share of pure direct_answer responses stays roughly flat to declining in relative rank while multi-part comic structures (setup_punchline, disagreement_humor, agreement_escalation) become proportionally more common. Short responses skew toward direct_answer/question_question/emotional_response (single-beat reactions); long responses skew toward layered comic or argumentative structures with a setup and payoff.

typical_context_by_structure.direct_answer: OBSERVED (from sample reading): dominant when last_speaker asks a concrete factual or logistical question (trivia, whereabouts, confirmations); most common in short responses.
typical_context_by_structure.observation_punchline: INFERRED: the single most common *comic* structure overall; triggered by an absurd, awkward, or emotionally loaded situation Chandler comments on with a one-line ironic tag, often standalone (single sentence).
typical_context_by_structure.question_question: INFERRED: frequent when Chandler is deflecting, clarifying, or reacting with disbelief/surprise to the prior line; common opener style even in short responses.
typical_context_by_structure.setup_punchline: INFERRED: concentrated in long responses (18% of long bucket vs 7% overall); typically an anecdote, hypothetical, or extended riff building to a twist in the final clause/sentence.
typical_context_by_structure.disagreement_humor: INFERRED: skews toward long responses and toward emotionally charged or accusatory prior lines; Chandler contradicts the premise while making it funny rather than confrontational.
typical_context_by_structure.agreement_escalation: INFERRED: appears across all buckets; Chandler nominally agrees with or extends the prior speaker's point/bit, then pushes it further for comic effect.
typical_context_by_structure.teasing: INFERRED: rises with response length (10% short -> 14% medium -> 13% long); usually targets a friend's stated flaw, romantic situation, or vanity.
typical_context_by_structure.callback: INFERRED: low frequency (3.8%) but structurally distinct - references a running gag or earlier established fact from context/backstory rather than the immediate prior line; cannot be fully verified without episode metadata, so confidence is lower.
typical_context_by_structure.reassurance: INFERRED: clusters around contexts where last_speaker expresses distress or vulnerability (see cross-tab with intent data); often paired with an undercutting joke rather than delivered straight.
typical_context_by_structure.emotional_response: INFERRED: common in short responses (18%); a direct affective reaction (surprise, hurt, alarm) without much elaboration.
typical_context_by_structure.topic_shift: INFERRED: frequently used as an avoidance/comfort mechanism after an uncomfortable or emotionally exposed line from another speaker.
typical_context_by_structure.deflection: INFERRED: appears with self-protective or awkward personal topics (being caught in a lie, accusations, embarrassing questions).
typical_context_by_structure.clarification: INFERRED: short, low-word-count responses; genuine requests for missing information rather than rhetorical.
typical_context_by_structure.correction: INFERRED: low frequency; used to fix a factual error in what was just said, sometimes combined with mild challenge.
typical_context_by_structure.conversational_continuation: INFERRED: minimal-content responses (greetings, filler acknowledgments) that keep the exchange going without adding new material.
typical_context_by_structure.conversational_repair: INFERRED: rare; self-interruption or trailing off mid-thought, often when a topic becomes emotionally difficult or a joke is abandoned.
typical_context_by_structure.self_correction: INFERRED: rare (1.3%); Chandler revises or undercuts his own preceding statement, often for a second comic beat.
typical_context_by_structure.refusal: INFERRED: rare; direct non-compliance, sometimes softened with humor.
typical_context_by_structure.uncertainty: INFERRED: rare as a *structure* (distinct from the intent 'express_uncertainty', which is more common); appears as hedged, unresolved phrasing.
typical_context_by_structure.qualification: INFERRED: rare; adds a conditional or caveat to an otherwise plain statement, frequently to set up an ironic undercut.
typical_context_by_structure.answer_joke: INFERRED: a direct answer immediately extended with a joke clause in the same response; concentrated in short/medium responses.
typical_context_by_structure.question_answer: INFERRED: low count in this tagging pass because most Q+A cases were tagged under direct_answer/question_question instead; treat as a lower-confidence, likely-undercounted category.
typical_context_by_structure.statement_rhetorical_q: INFERRED: a declarative frame collapses into a rhetorical question, frequently used to tease or challenge; associated with rhetorical-question-opener timing pattern (see Phase 13 file).

structure: speaker states an observation about the situation
speaker appends a short ironic or deflating tag
speaker opens an anecdote or hypothetical
final clause delivers an unexpected comic twist
speaker nominally agrees with prior point
speaker extends the idea further than intended for comic effect
speaker contradicts the premise of the prior line
contradiction is phrased as a joke rather than a straight rebuttal
speaker gives a literal answer to the question
speaker appends a short humorous aside in the same response
speaker responds to a statement or question with a new question
new question redirects, deflects, or expresses disbelief
prior line raises an uncomfortable or emotional topic
speaker responds with an unrelated, lower-stakes topic or request
speaker opens with a sincere reassuring statement
speaker closes with a joke that partially undercuts the sincerity

multi_label_note: OBSERVED: responses frequently exhibit 2 discourse structures simultaneously (e.g. teasing + observation_punchline, or direct_answer + answer_joke); percentages above are per-category incidence, not mutually exclusive shares, so they sum to well over 100%.
